 Fantasy Share Fantasy NFL Air Yards Report For Week 11 Fantasy Football
 Adam Pfeifer highlights three standouts in the air yards department to watch for ahead of Week 11.
 Adam Pfeifer 2d ago Share Published Nov 17, 2026, 4:40 PM ET Updated Nov 17, 2026, 4:40 PM ET 
 There’s perhaps nothing more tilting in fantasy football than unrealized air yards, but they do help paint a picture. Every Tuesday here at Fantasy Life, I’ll be highlighting some pass catchers who stood out in the air yards department for the given week.
 Let’s take a look at what happened last week.

 Fantasy Football Week 11 - Air Yards Report 
 Xavier Hutchinson | WR | Houston Texans 
 Week 10 air yards : 129 (11th)
 During the week, Houston QB C.J. Stroud talked about how important Hutchinson is to the Texans. And on Sunday, Stroud continued to lean on Hutchinson, targeting him nine times against Cleveland. Hutchinson caught just four of those targets for 58 yards, though he did find the end zone. His 129 air yards ranked top-12 among all pass-catchers this past week, but only 17 of those air yards were deemed catchable. Against Cleveland’s aggressive Cover-1 scheme, Stroud consistently took shots down the field, especially in the second half. But after a hot start to the game, Stroud only completed three passes. 
 Overall, Hutchinson has been quietly strong this season, and has now found the end zone in each of his last three games. He’s also seen at least five targets in all but one game, making him a viable FLEX/WR3 play in Week 11, especially with six teams on bye. 
 Elic Ayomanor | WR | Tennessee Titans 
 Week 10 air yards : 93 (15th)
 Let’s stay in the AFC South, shall we?
 With Carnell Tate and eventually Wan’Dale Robinson sidelined last week, Ayomanor emerged as Tennessee’s leading receiver, catching 5-of-10 targets for 79 yards. He flirted with 100 air yards on the day and while the Titans may be looked at as a gross offense for fantasy, they are actually a very fantasy-friendly scheme.
 Brian Daboll has really pushed the pace as of late. Since Week 6, the Titans easily lead the NFL in no-huddle rate (33%), while playing at the league’s second-fastest overall pace. Only the Eagles and Cowboys are averaging more plays per minute than the Titans (2.2) during that stretch, giving us more play volume for fantasy. If Tennessee is missing Tate and/or Robinson this Sunday against the Cowboys, Ayomanor would absolutely enter the WR3 discussion in fantasy leagues, especially given how fast both the Titans and Cowboys play on offense.
 George Pickens | WR | Dallas Cowboys 
 Week 10 air yards : 295 (1st)
 Speaking of the Cowboys, Pickens finally had a monster game last week, catching 11 of a career-high 18 targets for 145 yards and three touchdowns. His 295 air yards were easily the most in the NFL this past week, but also the most by any player all season long. Pickens is still running go routes 27% of the time this season, up from his 21.9% rate last season. But it worked out against San Francisco, a defense that deploys single-high coverage at one of the highest rates in the league. But Dallas clearly made it a point to get him involved early and often, as Pickens ran more in-breaking routes than he typically does.
 Pickens is always going to be heavily featured on vertical routes from the boundary. That’s not going to change. But the key to really unlocking his upside is for the Cowboys to not forget that he is still very dangerous on quick slants and in-breaking routes, too.
